CREATE2 gives both, subject to three ways of getting it wrong, all of which are handled and tested here: 1. **Address collision.** Two different init codes can hash to the same address. CREATE2    silently returns the existing contract instead of failing, so a deployment \"succeeds\"    while deploying nothing. `deploy` therefore reverts when the target already holds code,    and checks the result after the fact rather than trusting the return value. 2. **Constructor arguments are part of the init code, not the salt.** Two deployments that    differ only in a constructor argument have *different* addresses even with the same    salt. Salting on `(assetId, version)` alone would not make an address a stable function    of the asset. `saltFor` therefore also commits to the init code hash. 3. **The deploying address is part of the address.** The same salt from a different    factory yields a different address. `predict` therefore takes the factory, and the    factory rejects any attempt to use an address other than its own.","version":1}},"settings":{"compilationTarget":{"src/AidFactory.sol":"AidFactory"},"evmVersion":"cancun","libraries":{},"metadata":{"bytecodeHash":"ipfs"},"optimizer":{"enabled":true,"runs":200},"remappings":[]},"sources":{"src/AidFactory.sol":{"keccak256":"0x43e9f5f827233e70956d401609ba2b4b5d72362b4948fb7e9e13d12fc7ba37e5","license":"MIT","urls":["bzz-raw://ee9fa1e53e9f783bb5acfe76f6c8265f5eaa8d7dbe85c49a8affe275cc7219f9","dweb:/ipfs/QmQM2yRrbojhg11DWBq5F8NxCym7pihrnnmB9f6uduYWZh"]}},"version":1}

params.initCode: full creation code, including constructor arguments Returns the deployed address. Reverts if the target already has code — without that check, a second deployment of the same salt returns an address that looks like a success and contains a different, older contract.
params.salt: any 32-byte salt; use saltFor() for per-asset deployments

predict(bytes32,bytes32).details: Standard CREATE2 derivation: keccak256(0xff ++ factory ++ salt ++ initCodeHash).      View-only, so it can be called before anything exists.

params.assetId: the AID this deployment belongs to
params.initCodeHash: hash of the exact init code, so the salt commits to it Commits to the init code because CREATE2's address is a function of (deployer, salt, keccak256(initCode)). A salt that ignored the init code would let two different contracts share one address, which is the collision from point 1 arriving by a different route.

deployForAsset(bytes32,bytes).notice: Deploys a contract for a specific asset, using saltFor() for the salt. The assetId is recorded in the salt so that a caller can later prove an address belongs to an asset without trusting their own bookkeeping.

isDeployed(bytes32,bytes32).notice: True when the predicted address holds code — i.e. a deployment already exists.

predict(bytes32,bytes32).notice: The address a given (salt, initCodeHash) pair will produce from this factory.

predictForAsset(bytes32,bytes32).notice: Convenience: the address this asset's deployment will have.
